data.title: Idi Amin's grandson disqualified from Commonwealth boxing bout
data.description: GLASGOW - The grandson of former Ugandan president Idi Amin saw his bid for Commonwealth boxing gold end in disgrace as Aziz Abdul was disqualified for a headbutt in his quarter-final on Wednesday.

data.title: Principal reaction to FIFA's private investor plan
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - FIFA's plans to sell a stake in the business operations of the World Cup and its other competitions through the creation of a semi-private subsidiary has sparked disbelief and outrage globally.

data.title: O'Connor wins Commonwealth heptathlon as Australia set new record for swimming golds
data.description: GLASGOW - Kate O'Connor cruised to heptathlon gold for Northern Ireland as Australia rounded off their best ever Commonwealth Games in the pool with nine more swimming gold medals on Wednesday for a total of 37.

data.title: AI strategy now 'falling behind'
data.description: Thailand must develop its own Thai-language AI systems or risk falling behind foreign technology companies, economists and digital policy experts have warned.

data.title: Water security fears grow
data.description: A series of emerging reports in recent weeks concerning tight water supplies and river pollution in central and northern Thailand mean the nation is now facing a challenging water security situation, experts say.

data.title: Supanida snaps losing run to reach last 16
data.description: Supanida Katethong finally ended her first round losing spell when the Thai left-hander won her opening match at the US$250,000 (approx 8.4 million baht) BWF Taipei Open on Wednesday.

data.title: Thailand back to hard graft after day off
data.description: Thailand's national team were back on the training pitch at BGTC 3 on Wednesday, stepping up preparations for their Group B second fixture against Malaysia in the Asean Hyundai Cup 2026.

data.title: Ministry pushes Chumphon-Ranong rail
data.description: The Transport Ministry has pushed for the Chumphon-Ranong double-track railway project, describing the 110-kilometre route as a missing link needed to connect Thailand's rail network with an Andaman Sea port.

data.title: Flood diversion canal hits new flak
data.description: A civic network in Nakhon Nayok is stepping up its campaign against the proposed Pasak–Gulf of Thailand flood diversion canal, accusing authorities of misrepresenting the outcome of public consultations and downplaying strong local resistance to the project.

data.title: Dialogue offers path to peace
data.description: Manila: Thailand and Cambodia should engage more at diplomatic levels to resolve ongoing conflicts, said Asean secretary-general Kao Kim Hourn.

data.title: BTS pulls out of Grammys after Asian pop category introduction
data.description: SEOUL - Global K-pop sensation BTS said on Wednesday they will not submit their music for next year's Grammy Awards, following the Recording Academy's introduction of new categories that include the Best Asian Pop Music Performance.

data.title: No Thais hurt in Japan quake
data.description: The Foreign Affairs Ministry has activated emergency contact channels for Thai citizens in Japan following the magnitude 7.1 earthquake that struck Kumamoto Prefecture on Tuesday.

data.title: Asean envoy plans to visit Myanmar
data.description: Manila: Theresa P Lazaro, secretary of foreign affairs of the Philippines and the Asean Chair's Special Envoy on Myanmar, said she is scheduled to make a humanitarian visit to Myanmar in the fourth quarter of this year.

data.title: OPDC eyes some branch office closures
data.description: The Office of the Public Sector Development Commission (OPDC) will propose closing provincial branch offices of state agencies as part of an overhaul of the public administration system.

data.title: Spanish wildfire evacuees go home as France hit by new heat alert
data.description: ALDEA DEL FRESNO (SPAIN) - Thousands who fled huge wildfires in Spain returned home on Wednesday while in France firefighters braced for worsening conditions in their own battle with raging flames.

data.title: Nigeria dismantles meth lab, but fears of Mexican cartel links linger
data.description: IJEBU ODE (NIGERIA) - The cooking cauldrons and vats of chemicals were left behind in an abandoned shed, hidden in a Nigerian forest -- remnants of an alleged multimillion-dollar transnational meth operation.

data.title: Survivors still sought as Japan quake death toll hits 13
data.description: YATSUSHIRO, Japan - Rescuers frantically searched for ‌survivors on Wednesday, a day after a 7.1-magnitude earthquake shook southern Japan, killing at least 13 people, knocking out power to thousands of homes and rupturing roads across the region.

data.title: Oscar-winning musician Glen Hansard dies in motorcycle crash
data.description: DUBLIN - The Irish musician Glen Hansard, who won a Best Original Song Oscar in 2008 for the indie film “Once”, died in a motorcycle crash at the age ​of 56 early on ⁠Wednesday, his management company said.

data.title: Suspects sought in young Russians’ disappearance flee
data.description: CHON BURI - Police surrounded a house in Bang Lamung district on Wednesday in an attempt to arrest two men believed to be connected to the disappearance of two Russian siblings from Pattaya, but the suspects had already fled.

data.title: Thai YouTuber ‘Hlun Solo’ found dead in Georgia
data.description: The Thai travel YouTuber “Hlun Solo” has been found dead in a hotel room in Tbilisi, the capital of Georgia, more than two weeks after his family last had contact with him.

data.title: The photo that sums up Europe’s wildfire summer
data.description: PARIS - AFP photo editor Maximilien Lamy was on holiday with his partner and daughter last week when he took a series of snapshots of vacationers in fire-struck southwestern France with his smartphone.

data.title: Koh Samui faces water rationing
data.description: A shortage of tap water has led to rationing on Koh Samui, where a prolonged dry spell has reduced clean water production capacity to about 40% of normal levels, according to the Provincial Waterworks Authority (PWA).

data.title: US Senate confirms Clayton as Trump intelligence chief
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The US Senate has confirmed Jay Clayton as President Donald Trump's top intelligence official, putting a permanent chief in charge of the country's spy agencies as the president revives unsupported election fraud claims ahead of the midterms.

data.title: US and Saudis strike Iraq militants in expanding war
data.description: BAGHDAD - US and Saudi forces said they struck an Iraqi militant alliance on Wednesday, as the Middle East war expands beyond its main focus in Iran to involve the Islamic republic’s proxies.

data.title: Spanish wildfire evacuees start returning home
data.description: ALDEA DEL FRESNO, Spain - Thousands of Spaniards evacuated from the path of huge wildfires were returning home on Wednesday while in France firefighters braced for worsening conditions in their own battle with raging flames.

data.title: Pub fire probe nears completion as death toll rises to 37
data.description: Police investigating the deadly Rong Beer Na Ladprao pub fire in Bangkok say they are close to completing their inquiries, as the death toll rose to 37 after another injured victim succumbed to her injuries on Wednesday.

data.title: Search stepped up for missing Thai YouTuber in Georgia
data.description: Thailand’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs is closely monitoring efforts to locate the travel YouTuber “Hlun Solo”, who has been out of contact with his family for more than two weeks since travelling to Georgia to film content.

data.title: Chinese man held in counterfeit cosmetics case
data.description: A Chinese national has been arrested after police raided a warehouse in Muang district of Samut Prakan and seized more than 18,000 counterfeit cosmetics and personal care products bearing fake trademarks of well-known brands.

data.title: Illuminating Faith: Ubon’s Candle Festival Marks 125 Years
data.description: Glowing wax floats, pop-art landmarks, and light shows transform Ubon Ratchathani into E-san’s premier cultural showcase this July

data.title: New Thai FDA rules tighten adverts for supplements and infant food
data.description: Effective Tuesday (July 28, 2026), the rules ban misleading claims, set age limits for models and restrict adverts for infant foods and certain supplements.

data.title: ‘Not as advertised’ room shock resolved in Nan
data.description: NAN - A father and son on holiday got an unpleasant surprise after finding their room did not come close to matching what they had booked, but a prompt response ensured their stay was not spoiled.

data.title: Russian wanted for B600,000 theft from safe in Phuket
data.description: PHUKET - Police are hunting a Russian man who they say broke into a safe at a currency exchange counter and made off with foreign currency worth around 600,000 baht.

data.title: Thai soldier loses foot to landmine in Sa Kaeo
data.description: SA KAEO: A Thai soldier lost his foot when he stepped on a landmine during a clearance mission in Ban Nong Chan village of Khok Sung district in Sa Kaeo province late Wednesday morning.

data.title: ONE Championship: Dayakaev vows to prove he is ‘complete’ fighter by beating Superlek again
data.description: Abdulla Dayakaev wants to turn one controversial victory over Superlek into an undeniable statement at The Inner Circle 25 – and prove he possesses far more than the punching power that made his name.

data.title: Thousands of fake products seized in Min Buri
data.description: Police have seized more than 32,000 counterfeit branded products from a Bangkok warehouse reportedly run by a Chinese national who imported the goods from China and sold them online at heavily discounted prices.

data.title: PM Anutin to visit Indonesia next week
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul will make an official visit to Indonesia on Aug 3 and 4 to hold talks aimed at strengthening ties between the two Southeast Asian nations.

data.description: Looking for a title to binge-watch this weekend? Here's our pick!

data.title: Hong Kong bookstores closing after ‘sedition’ raids
data.description: HONG KONG - A Hong Kong bookshop raided by national security police earlier this month announced on Wednesday that it would close after 50 years in business, while another has shut down ahead of schedule.
